shape_hint: Headless (grub) screw: a plain threaded cylinder with a hexagon socket (key size s, depth t) cut into one end and a shaped point at the other end - flat (dia dp), cone (small tip), dog (full-length cylinder dp, length z) or cup (concave end, rim dia dz). Thread runs the full length; a short chamfer at the socket end.

role_map.t_min_short: min key engagement depth for short lengths
role_map.t_min_long: min key engagement depth for long lengths
role_map.dp_max: max diameter of flat point and of dog point

notes: Values are valid for DIN 913/914/915/916 and ISO 4026/4027/4028/4029 where they overlap. t_min_short/long apply to flat (913/4026), dog (915/4028) and cup (916/4029); for the cone type DIN 914 sources give t M12 = 4.5 (3 sources) instead of 4.8. Parsed all into 4 point types and pooled values across types (they are identical in the standards). Matrix 13 rows x 6 cols x 6 clusters. Min clusters: P 4, s 5, t_min_short 3, t_min_long 3, dp_max 5, dz_max 5. Dissent: lexikon DIN 916 M4 s '12' (typo), ita DIN 915 M10 t '4/3' (typo; torq 4/6), ITT+B M12 t_short 4.5 for DIN 914 (and ITT for DIN 916). Semantics: t short/long confirmed by headers 'short/long' (aya), 'Short screw/Long screw' (gf 4027), footnote L<=L0 short (gf 4026). dz<=dp<d, t_short<t_long, monotone: pass.
problems: t_min_short / t_min_long are supported by exactly 3 clusters on all 13 rows (F, G, ITT; B adds short only M2-M20 flat). All three are catalogue/aggregator style pages; ita+torq treated as ONE cluster, gf+aya as ONE cluster.

M12 t_min_short=4.8 is contested by type: 4.8 on fasten.it (all 8 pages), gf (4026/4027), aya, boltsfastener 913/916, ita/torq 913/915; but 4.5 on ita+torq DIN 914 and DIN 916 and boltsfastener DIN 914. For the cone type (DIN 914/ISO 4027) it is 2 vs 2 clusters; cup (4029) only fasten.it+boltsf agree. The record's note admits this only for the cone type. Flat/dog/cup-ISO values are fine; if the family must hold for all 4 point types strictly, drop the M12 t_min_short cell (or row M12).
